title: NBA YoungBoy Is Giving Sobriety a Chance: ‘I’m Trying to See if I Really Can Make It to 6 Months’
summary: The Louisiana rapper moved to South Korea and is trying to stay clean and out of trouble.
body: YoungBoy Never Broke Again is going to give the sober life a try. The Louisiana rapper took to his Instagram Stories and shared that he flushed the rest of the drugs he had down the toilet and is going to try to be sober for six consecutive months. “I wanted to get high last night I just flushed the sh– down the toilet,” he said. “I’m trying to see if I really can make it to 6 months.” He also posted an IG Story hinting at a new album. “Hope yall ready for my album,” he told his followers. “This when we separate this and that.” Back in 2023, he told Bootleg Kev that he had checked himself into a rehab facility during an interview. “I went to rehab for a weekend recently,” he admitted. “I still get an image that I do a lot of drugs, so I kinda get that thrown in my face like, ‘This is taking over his mind or something.” NBA, who now lives in South Korea, recently sat down with Funny Marco and hinted at retirement and revealed that he has no interest in moving back to the United States anytime soon. “I’ll go on tour one more time throughout my whole life and that’s it,” he said before saying that he has “one or two&#8…

title: Ariana Grande Slams Trump Administration for Using ‘We Can’t Be Friends’ in TikTok Video: ‘Your Truth Is False’
summary: The pop star previously blasted the Trump administration in June for using "Bye" in a TikTok clip.
body: Ariana Grande has once again blasted the Trump administration for using her music in social media clips promoting the president. Team Trump posted a video to TikTok on Thursday (Aug. 20) soundtracked by Grande’s 2024 Eternal Sunshine hit “We Can’t Be Friends (Wait for Your Love).” The clip finds Trump walking toward the podium at a speaking engagement and is captioned with lyrics from Grande’s Billboard Hot 100 -topping smash, “Me and my truth we sit in silence,” followed by a statement about women’s sports. “Men can’t have babies and should never compete in women’s sports,” the post continues. Team Trump added in the caption: “This shouldn’t be controversial! #trump #arianagrande #maga.” Grande quickly got wind of Team Trump’s post and slammed the administration for using her work in the comment section. “Never use my music again. Also, your truth is false,” she responded. Arianators also flocked to the comment section to alert the singer. “Does Ariana know he’s using her song AGAIN,” one fan wrote. title: Kenny Chesney Fan Who Paid $300K to an Imposter Cannot Sue The Real Country Star, Court Says
summary: A woman claimed the star himself was legally liable after she was scammed by a phony Kenny Chesney on the internet.
body: A woman who was scammed out of more than $300,000 by a Kenny Chesney impersonator can’t sue the country superstar, an appeals court says. Patricia Linson, who paid $310,000 to a phony Chesney after he told her he was “experiencing financial difficulties,” claimed that the real star was legally liable for failing to stop imposters from defrauding his fans. Related Kenny Chesney Rewrites Top 10 Record on Country Airplay Chart With ‘Carry On’ HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery BE:FIRST Is Ready for the World: Inside the J-Pop Superstars' Long-Planned U.S. Breakthrough But in a ruling last week obtained by Billboard , a California appeals court ruled that legal precedent does not “require celebrities to warn and protect their fans against third-party imposter scams.” “We do not doubt that financial scams are becoming more sophisticated and prevalent as technological developments make it easier for people to impersonate others,” the court wrote in the Aug 11 ruling. “[But] it would stretch the [the law] beyond what is supported by common sense and sound public policy to require celebrities to post warnings about third-party scams on their web…
